summary.headline: Mrs. Bectors Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14.3% YoY to ₹630.5 crore, with EBITDA margin (Habitat) steady at 13.1% despite cost inflation.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was a record ₹630.5 crore, up 14.3% YoY and 14.9% QoQ, with Habitat (EBITDA) of ₹82.5 crore up 19.1% and margin at 13.1%, up 50 bps YoY and flat QoQ. PAT was ₹45.7 crore, up about 25% YoY, with PAT margin at 7.3% versus 6.6%. H1 FY27 revenue was ₹1,179.3 crore (+15.1%), Habitat ₹154.6 crore (+21.2%, margin 13.1%, +70 bps) and PAT ₹84.5 crore (+25.4%). Gross margin fell about 1 percentage point QoQ from raw material and packaging inflation, and management expects pressure to persist into Q3.

segments.name: Biscuits (domestic)
segments.commentary: Domestic biscuit volume grew about 4-5% (mid-single digit), value growth in low teens. Distribution targeted at 40,000 new outlets (₹245+ billing) within 400-500 km of Rajkot; about 30,000 added so far, with outlets now near 345,000.

segments.name: Bakery (English Oven, Nature Baked)
segments.commentary: Bakery grew in high teens to 20s; management cited value growth in high teens to 20s and volume mid-teens. Quick commerce is now the largest reach driver and organised trade contributes 43-44% of bakery; Q-com is about 22% of combined bakery and biscuit revenue. Bakery is about twice the size of institutional bakery.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export grew but slower in Q2 given West Asia shipping disruption, vessel availability and freight rates; management says order cycles were delayed and FY outlook is mid-teens growth.

segments.name: Institutional bakery
segments.commentary: Recovering, with growth lagging English Oven; management expects trend change this financial year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 revenue growth in the mid-teens, with H2 forecast at mid-to-high teens.
Q3 Habitat margin targeted at 13-13.5% (maintained at Q2 levels); Q4 targeted at close to 14%, with a medium-term target of 14-15%.
Price increase of about 3% taken in Q2 (QoQ); a further price increase in October, with full-year FY27 price increase of roughly 5-6%.
Management expects margins to stay under pressure in the near term, with recovery building as price increases, annual savings and Project Impact mature.
Volume growth in domestic biscuits targeted to move from 4-5% toward high single digit and then double digit over the next few quarters.
capex_capacity: New Kolkata and Khopoli (Maharashtra) bakery units are scaling up; Khopoli commissioned this year, to drive distribution in Maharashtra.
Partner unit started in Lucknow; North vs rest-of-India revenue mix expected to stay around 80:20.
Bakery capacity: management prefers in-house over outsourcing for quality; Mumbai adequate for a couple of years, Punjab may need capacity; targeting about 20% growth.
Private outlets (premium outlets) contribute 13-14% and are targeted to reach 20%.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand resilient, led by premium and value-added products, modern trade, quick commerce and institutional recovery; below-normal monsoon and food inflation weighed on rural sentiment.
India CPI inflation rose from about 4.4% in June to 5.5% in September 2026, driven by edible oils, sugar and cereals.
Biscuit price parity with the best of competition now achieved; price increases in Q2 and Q3 driven by commodities.
Gross margin decline of about 1 pp QoQ due to raw material and packaging costs; freight and fuel costs raised other expenses.

Competition intense in North biscuits from large and regional players; new startups entering quick commerce bakery. Quick commerce innovation: 5 new products and two seasonal collaborations planned for festive period.

qa_highlights.question: How is competition intensity in North India biscuits, and what is the distribution plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Intensity is high from large and regional players; distribution target of 40,000 outlets added within 400-500 km of Rajkot, with about 30,000 added and about 345,000 outlets. 10-15% more distributors added; premium variants on quick commerce, with biscuit growth in low teens.

qa_highlights.question: Shape of bakery growth in retail and institutional channels, and export trends?
qa_highlights.answer: English Oven volume grew mid-to-high teens and value high teens to 20s; institutional bakery lags but is recovering. Exports slowed on West Asia shipping delays, but management says customer relationships are strong and FY growth is mid-teens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 price increase and growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3% price increase taken in Q2 (partly late in quarter), with the balance in Q3. Full-year price increase expected at around 5-6%. H2 growth forecast at mid-to-high teens.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin decline breakup and Q3/Q4 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Decline is a mix of raw material and packaging costs; recovery in pricing was about one quarter behind. Q3 margin target maintained at about 13-13.1%, Q4 near 14%. About 70% of biscuit volume is in the ₹5 and ₹10 packs, with recovery via grammage changes.

qa_highlights.question: Is quick commerce margin accretive for bakery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q-com margins are better due to planning efficiency, although marketing spend there is higher. Long-term margin impact depends on brand investment and capacity mix.

qa_highlights.question: Volume trend and price parity in biscuits?
qa_highlights.answer: Price parity with competition achieved; volume growth about 4-5%, driven by distribution expansion and throughput per outlet. Target to move to high single digit and then double digit.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (edible oil, packaging, freight) pressuring gross margin, with Q3 described as the steepest cost quarter.
West Asia conflict affecting vessel availability, freight rates and export order timing.
Rural demand weakness from below-normal monsoon and sharp food inflation; possible consumer trading down in bread.
Competition in North biscuits and new startups in quick commerce bakery.
Leadership transition: domestic biscuit business now overseen by Suvib Bector; succession plan not yet finalised; new CFO recently joined.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term margins and the environment, but confident on growth, pricing discipline and the Q4 margin recovery target. Management was candid that the quarter was tougher than expected and avoided firm commitments on Q3 beyond maintaining margins.

adds.what: Khopoli (Maharashtra) bakery unit, commissioned this year
New Kolkata bakery unit scaling up

growth.why: Management reiterates FY27 revenue growth in the mid-teens (H2 mid-to-high teens), backed by pricing (~5-6% FY27 price increases), 40,000-outlet distribution expansion (about 30,000 added so far), and new Khopoli/Kolkata/Lucknow units, but no specific new capacity volumes or order numbers were quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Habitat margin held at 13.1% in Q2 after a ~1 pp QoQ gross margin drop; management targets 13-13.5% in Q3 and close to 14% in Q4, with ~3% price hike taken in Q2 and a further ~5-6% full-year price increase, though Q3 is the steepest cost quarter.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Khopoli is commissioned and Kolkata is in trial runs, but no capacity volumes or dates were quantified; management says Mumbai is adequate for a couple of years and Punjab 'may need' capacity against ~20% bakery growth target.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Domestic biscuit volume grows ~4-5% today with a target to move to high single digit then double digit, backed by ~30,000 of 40,000 planned new outlets added (about 345,000 total); bakery volume is mid-teens.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure was given and no board-level capex was announced; Punjab bakery capacity may be needed in the medium term given the ~20% growth target.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance was held at mid-teens (H2 mid-to-high teens), and management described Q2 as tougher than expected with exports slowed by West Asia shipping disruption.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management avoided firm Q3 margin commitments beyond holding 13-13.5%, CPI rose from ~4.4% to 5.5%, and commodity and freight costs remain elevated while pricing lags by about a quarter.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans 5 new quick-commerce products and two seasonal collaborations for the festive period.

rows.label: Export recovery as order cycles resume
rows.why: Exports grew slower in Q2 on West Asia shipping delays and freight rates, but management still expects FY27 growth in the mid-teens and says order cycles were only delayed.

rows.label: Second price hike in October; ~5-6% FY27 total
rows.why: About 3% was taken in Q2 and a further increase was announced for October, with full-year FY27 pricing of roughly 5-6%.

rows.label: Institutional bakery recovery
rows.why: Management expects a trend change in institutional bakery this FY, though it still lags English Oven growth (high teens to 20s).

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, pricing discipline and the Q4 14% margin target but cautious on Q3 margins, commodity inflation and West Asia export disruption; analysts pressed on North India competition, margin recovery and quick-commerce profitability.
